input.quote: 8.1 This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms.
input.rationale: The term is three years, and Section 9 provides only for-cause (9.1), insolvency (9.2), and Vendor-failure (9.3) termination; Sections 6.2, 19.4, 20.5 and 27.3 are likewise all cause- or event-based. No Customer termination-for-convenience right exists anywhere, which is walk-away territory for a multi-year term. Section 8.2 (180 days' non-renewal notice) is natural-term non-renewal under RENEWAL, not a convenience right, and is not flagged here. Vendor is given no convenience right either, but no express words confirm that, so we state it in the same inserted clause. We propose a new 9.4 at the preferred level: 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; 60 days' notice remains available as a fallback.

proposal.summary: Insert new Section 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience termination right with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and confirming Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 9 gives us only for-cause and insolvency exits, so we are locked into a three-year term with no convenience right. We have added a new 9.4 allowing us to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and confirming Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term; if helpful we can move to 60 days' notice as a fallback.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund prepaid fees pro rata for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
